analysis: All three supplied units are base-side text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (start lines 855, 1191, 1582). They are documentation only. No patch hunks were included, so the actual added or removed lines in this PR are not visible to me. The excerpts hold release notes and contain no executable code, auth logic, crypto, billing or configuration. I found no concrete security regression in them. The notes touch the SSD prefix cache and the encrypted-at-rest checkpoint tier, which maps to T-041/SEC-035. They also mention the 100 GiB SSD cache ceiling, which differs from the threat model's default of available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling, and the v0.9.0 candidate notes. That is pre-existing text, not a change I can attribute to this PR. The next pass should check the real diff of CHANGELOG.md, and any non-doc files in the PR, for behavior changes that claim or imply a security posture. Examples are SSD cache TTL, disk budget, scope derivation, App Attest or MDM serving authorization, and account-erasure behavior. Because the diff is missing, I treat this as a coverage limit and not as evidence the change is safe.
